messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Sudden spike in 5xx rates and per-token latency in us-west-2. Memory and open-kv entries for continuous-batcher jumped ~6x starting ~14:02 UTC. Paging maya_sre for on-call.

maya_sre: I'm on it. any quick graphs/queries?

dinesh_ml: checking traces now — seeing a ton of reused KV entries with wrong seq_offset header, looks like cross-request leakage when batcher reuses KVCache objects.

sam_runtime: ugh. that matches a risky optimization we rolled yesterday (kv_reuse=true + paged-kv). Could be stale keys when request_id isn't cleared before reuse.

emily_support: customer-facing: detection triggered for multiple customers — 5 enterprise queries timeouts, several small apps saw elevated latencies. Notified top 3 customers already.

maya_sre: ok first mitigation: disable KV reuse for continuous-batcher on prod canary pool. I can flip runtime flag via ops-admin. prepping command.

sam_runtime: thanks. if we disable reuse, throughput will drop but ought to avoid correctness leakage. Also consider temporary lowering batch_max_tokens to reduce memory blowup.

maya_sre: executing now:
```
# disable kv reuse for continuous-batcher in canary pool
curl -X POST https://ops-admin.internal/v1/config -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN' -d '{"pool":"cb-canary-usw2","overrides":{"kv_cache_reuse":false,"batch_max_tokens":1024}}'
```

incident-bot: action recorded: config update queued (req id 9f3c). Rolling to 5 nodes in cb-canary-usw2.

dinesh_ml: capturing example failing trace snippet: request A and request B share same kv_key ABC123 even though they were different sequences. seq_offset in header shows mismatch. Looks like object pool returned object with old keys not cleared.

sam_runtime: can we hotfix the object pool clear path? small patch to reset kv_map on checkout should be quick. I'll prepare a candidate.

sam_runtime: patch ready, will push to canary runtime only:
```
--- a/runtime/kv_pool.cpp
+++ b/runtime/kv_pool.cpp
@@
-  auto obj = pool.checkout();
+  auto obj = pool.checkout();
+  // ensure no stale entries survive reuse
+  obj->kv_map.clear();
+  obj->last_seq = 0;
```

maya_sre: can we shadow test the patch on 2 canary nodes before full rollout?

sam_runtime: yes. starting canary deploy.

incident-bot: canary deploy started at 14:12 UTC (deploy id: dpl-778). Monitoring health/p50/p95.

emily_support: I'll keep customers updated: ETA for mitigation?

maya_sre: initial mitigation (kv_reuse=false) applied at 14:10 UTC to canary, patch deploy at 14:13 UTC. Observing p95 latency drop and memory use stabilizing on canary nodes.

dinesh_ml: after canary patch p95 down 30%, no more seq_offset mismatches in sampled traces. Good sign.

ryan_oncall: I'm taking over live monitoring. maya — handoff in 15?

maya_sre: handing to ryan. I'll run the rollout to the rest of the pool with you on watch.

ryan_oncall: rolling to full pool now (cb-prod-usw2), plan: 20% -> 50% -> 100% with 2m observation windows.

incident-bot: rollout started at 14:20 UTC (rollout id: r-2248).

emily_support: customers reporting fewer errors already, one enterprise confirmed stability for their long-context eval endpoints.

sam_runtime: while we have the rollback and config flip, we should collect a reproducible unit test for the object pool reuse case. I'll write an integration that simulates overlapping requests and checks kv_map emptiness on checkout.

dinesh_ml: good call. also saving a corpus of failing traces and request payloads for postmortem.

incident-bot: alerts cleared at 14:43 UTC. final status: all cb-prod-usw2 nodes rolled out, kv_reuse disabled cluster-wide, patch staged for full deploy in next release.

maya_sre: timeline recap for postmortem:
- 14:02 UTC: anomaly detection triggered (memory + 5xx).
- 14:04 UTC: paging and triage started.
- 14:10 UTC: runtime flag kv_reuse=false applied to canary pool.
- 14:13 UTC: quick patch deployed to canary pool.
- 14:20 UTC: rollout to prod pool started.
- 14:43 UTC: alerts cleared, customer impact reduced to baseline.

emily_support: impact summary for follow-up: 12 customers saw increased latencies/timeouts, 3 had sustained 5xx for >5m, 0 data exfil required. support tickets created: INC-4512, INC-4513, INC-4514.

ryan_oncall: next actions (short):
- keep kv_reuse=false until full unit+integration tests land in stable release.
- schedule emergency release with object-pool clear patch (sam).
- add additional guardrails: verify seq_offset vs request_id on checkout (dinesh).

sam_runtime: will prepare release and CI tests. also adding a stress test to the nightly runner for paged-kv + high-concurrency batcher.

maya_sre: postmortem owners: sam_runtime (fix & release), dinesh_ml (regression test + trace corpus), ryan_oncall (monitoring + dashboards), emily_support (customer comms).

emily_support: drafting customer post-incident note now, will share in #customer-updates once reviewed.

dinesh_ml: investigation note: root cause appears to be a subtle race where checkout->populate->request assignment assumes fresh kv_map; earlier optimization skipped explicit clear for perf. under cornered reuse + paged eviction, stale entries were reachable. we'll include the exact repro in the postmortem.

maya_sre: thanks all. handing to ryan for the midnight-watch and follow-up.

ryan_oncall: acknowledged. I'll keep status in #incidents and ping if anything creeps back. closing thread once postmortem posted. :white_check_mark:
